risk: Contact-mix forecast error: Order & Delivery workload under-forecast while Returns/Payments is over-planned
evidence_from_simulation: Event-week OD workload +24% vs forecast; RP +1%; OD queue short in 46 group-hours while RP carries 544 surplus agent-hours
probability_basis: Computed: OD SLA below target in 100% of replications
impact_basis: OD queue is the bottleneck in the as-planned scenario; see evidence column for magnitude
mitigation_action: Re-forecast by queue using exception/stock-out signals; rebalance headcount between queues; cross-train for flex (S2, S4)
dependencies: Operations (exception feed) -> Workforce Planning -> Customer Support Team Leads
escalation_trigger: OD queue SLA < 70% for 2 consecutive hours OR backlog > 100 contacts

risk: Siloed skill queues prevent moving spare capacity to the bottleneck
evidence_from_simulation: RP queue had 544 surplus agent-hours while OD was short; cross-training lifts modelled SLA by +8.7 pp (MC mean)
probability_basis: Computed: event SLA below target in 96% of replications
impact_basis: Largest single modelled lever on OD SLA
mitigation_action: Cross-train 20% of agents (training time not modelled)
dependencies: Training -> Customer Support -> Workforce Planning (certification before E1)

risk: Delivery-delay contacts lag fulfilment exceptions by 1-2 days and are not in the order-based forecast
evidence_from_simulation: Exceptions peaked at 6,911 on E7; delivery_delay contacts rose +229% vs baseline avg day
probability_basis: Judgement: mechanism built into the simulation (1-2 day lag); materialises whenever exceptions spike
impact_basis: Drives the largest category-level forecast miss
mitigation_action: Daily exception-count feed to WFM; apply lagged contact-rate model to next-day forecast
dependencies: Fulfilment Ops -> Workforce Planning (daily data handoff by 10:00)
escalation_trigger: Late-shipment count > 2x baseline-day average OR carrier-disruption notice

risk: Backlog carry-over snowball: overnight backlog is not cleared before next day's peak
evidence_from_simulation: As-planned: end-of-event backlog > 50 contacts in 68% of replications; peak backlog 450 contacts
impact_basis: Backlog means repeat contacts and customer wait
mitigation_action: Targeted overflow capacity at OD evening peak (S4); morning recovery roster
dependencies: Customer Support -> Workforce Planning (recovery plan trigger)

risk: Approval lead time for additional capacity
evidence_from_simulation: S3/S4 need approved extra agents (420 extra paid agent-hours in the model)
impact_basis: Without approval, S3/S4/S5/S6 cannot be executed
mitigation_action: Submit capacity request with scenario evidence by T-14; agree decision date

risk: Late-event agent fatigue raises absence on E6-E7 (finale peak)
evidence_from_simulation: Absence assumed 8% on E6-E7 vs 6% baseline; E7 is the highest-demand day
mitigation_action: Rotate shifts, cap overtime, plan recovery days
escalation_trigger: Overtime > 10% of scheduled hours on any day

risk: Upstream fulfilment capacity exceeded / carrier disruption inflates exceptions
evidence_from_simulation: Orders exceeded fulfilment capacity on E1, E6, E7; carrier disruption days E4-E5
probability_basis: Judgement: modelled capacity limit is breached on peak days
mitigation_action: Pre-position inventory; carrier contingency; early customer comms
dependencies: Fulfilment Ops -> Customer Support (proactive comms) -> Workforce Planning
escalation_trigger: Orders > 95% of fulfilment capacity forecast OR carrier SLA breach

risk: Unscheduled evening deal drops shift intraday demand to 20:00-21:59
evidence_from_simulation: Event-week contacts at 20:00-21:59 +14% vs forecast profile; deal days: E1, E4, E7
impact_basis: Evening hours short but total headcount near balance
mitigation_action: Require 72-hour notice of deal drops; add peak-cover shift (S3/S4)
escalation_trigger: Deal not on approved promo calendar 24 h before launch

risk: Unplanned absence spike during the event
evidence_from_simulation: Absence assumed 12% on E3 vs 6% baseline; realised event-week absence 6.4% of scheduled shifts
probability_basis: Judgement: event-day absence is an assumption in the model
impact_basis: Each 1 pt of absence ~ 1 agent per 100 scheduled
mitigation_action: Standby/flex pool; overtime and shift-swap protocol; cross-training (S2)

risk: Forecast refresh cadence too slow to react in-event
mitigation_action: Twice-daily forecast vs actual review; rolling correction rule (S1)

risk: Shift-template mismatch: single late template covers the 19:00 peak while mid-day overlaps over-cover
evidence_from_simulation: Highest shortfall hours (event, OD): 19:00, 20:00, 11:00; reallocation within templates changed SLA by -0.5 pp (MC mean)
probability_basis: Judgement: structural to the template set
impact_basis: Template reshaping is a limited lever; see evidence column for the modelled S1 effect
mitigation_action: Add shifted-start templates / split shifts; evaluate before event
escalation_trigger: Shortfall in same hour on 3 consecutive days

risk: Promotion-driven AHT inflation not in plan
evidence_from_simulation: Actual AHT +4.1% vs planned across the event week
impact_basis: Modest per day, compounds with volume error
mitigation_action: Macro/FAQ updates for promo rules; track AHT daily; update planning AHT
